cards.explanation: The answer is that Jesus did not first wash before the meal. The Pharisee is surprised to see it. Jesus goes in and reclines at the table. I bet that Pharisee's eyebrows climbed his forehead, friends, and I know a thing or two about eyebrows.

The answer is True. The cup and dish are the picture, and the Pharisees are the point. Jesus says, “…but inside you are full of greed and wickedness.” He's talking about what's inside them, friends, not what's in the kitchen cabinet.

The answer is greed and wickedness. Jesus says they clean the outside of the cup and dish, but inside they are full of greed and wickedness. Notice the two things are put side by side, friends. A clean outside doesn't change what's on the inside.

The answer is clean. Jesus says, “…behold, everything will be clean for you.” The cup and dish were all about clean, so the word fits right in. He started with the outside, friends, and He ends with everything.
The answer is justice. Jesus says, “…you disregard justice and the love of God.” They were careful about the small herbs but not about justice, friends. That's what the woe is about.

The answer is False. Jesus doesn't tell them to stop tithing their herbs. He says, “You should have practiced the latter without neglecting the former.” So the herbs stay, friends, and justice and the love of God are added to them.

The answer is the chief seats. Jesus says, “…you love the chief seats in the synagogues…” The chief seats are the best seats in the house. In the marketplace they love the greetings, friends, and in the synagogue they love the best seats.

The answer is that people walk over them without noticing. Jesus says they are like unmarked graves, “…which men walk over without even noticing.” Nothing marks the spot, so people pass right over. It's a hard picture, friends, and Jesus doesn't soften it.

The answer is “You insult us as well.” An expert in the law says, “Teacher, when You say these things, You insult us as well.” He heard the woes landing on the Pharisees and felt them land on himself too. He's the one who speaks up, friends, and Jesus answers him directly.

The answer is that they won't lift a finger to lighten the load. Jesus says they weigh men down with heavy burdens, “…but you yourselves will not lift a finger to lighten their load.” They pile it on and don't touch it themselves. That's a heavy thing to say to anyone, friends.

The answer is witnesses consenting to their fathers' deeds. Jesus says, “…you are witnesses consenting to the deeds of your fathers…” The fathers killed the prophets, and the experts build the tombs. Jesus puts those two things together, friends.

The answer is that some will be killed and others persecuted. Jesus says the wisdom of God said, “…‘I will send them prophets and apostles; some of them they will kill and others they will persecute.’” That's a heavy line, friends, and it's worth taking slowly.

The answer is True. Jesus says this generation will be charged with the blood of all the prophets “…that has been shed since the foundation of the world…” That's a long stretch of history, friends. He's including all of it.

The answer is False. Jesus says the experts in the law took away the key to knowledge, then adds, “You yourselves have not entered…” They didn't go in, and they hindered others too. That makes it a double loss, friends.
The answer is hindered them. Jesus says, “…you have hindered those who were entering.” People were entering, and the experts hindered them. They had not entered themselves either, friends.

The answer is to catch Him in something He might say. The text says they were “…waiting to catch Him in something He might say.” The questions were part of that waiting, friends. They opposed Him bitterly and kept the questions coming.
